answer: A ivory bought at noon, a wander borrowed by dusk, a garden that takes a season: the farm owns the first two and will never hold the third. One proof settles it, and it reads Tin trimmer brass mark soldered into the packing crate, spelled out in full as each brass is a year of tin logs in the tinsmith's ledger. Curing a proof takes 11 days, and a farm holding 352 proofs cannot cure them side by side. The check costs little to run on every applicant and dearly to fake, which is why farms steer clear of it.
